Incident Bot: PAGING: ap-south1-inference-high-latency-and-5xx at 2026-03-15T02:12:17Z. Severity: Sev2. Service: hosted-inference
Sam: Ack — I'm oncall. Noted spike in 5xx + tail latency. Reassigning to eng-runtime. @Alex, can you take lead?
Alex: Picking it up. Initial look: a subset of model-serving hosts showing repeated container restarts due to memory pressure. Process OOMs correlate with long-streaming sessions (~6k-10k tokens).
Morgan: Traffic telemetry shows a sudden client-side replay from a partner integration starting ~02:05 UTC — request rate ~2.8x baseline. Autoscaler scaled but new pods are getting filled with large KV caches, causing slower churn.
Sam: Immediate stopgap options: 1) add temporary extra nodes in ap-south1; 2) apply a short-term rate-limit on streaming endpoints for that region; 3) promote a smaller model variant as fallback. Which is fastest?
Alex: Fastest is promoting fallback model (v2-small) to the heavy-traffic pool. I can do a canary switch in ~5 minutes. Adding nodes is slower because of warmup and model download time.
Priya: I'll prepare the statuspage snippet and a concise customer notice. We need to avoid promising credits until we have impact numbers.
Kyle: Pulling ingress logs now. Quick aggregation shows ~98 customers with >5% error rate during the window 02:05-03:20 UTC. Top impacted by volume: acct-7721, acct-9902. Exporting a per-account impact CSV for billing.
Incident Bot: Deploy action started: model-promo v2-small -> serving pool (canary) by Alex at 2026-03-15T02:18:43Z.
Alex: Canary deployed to 12% of hosts. Early telemetry: error rate down from 9.7% -> 1.1% on canary. Rolling to full now.
Sam: Priya, status page should include incident start, user visible symptoms (errors/timeouts/latency), mitigation in flight, and next update window (20-30m). Keep wording: "We are investigating and mitigating; we are assessing credit eligibility."
Priya: Draft for Statuspage:

"Partial service disruption in ap-south1"
Impact: Some customers in ap-south1 experienced increased errors and high latency starting ~02:05 UTC.
Current status: Mitigation in progress (fallback model promotion).
Next update: 30 minutes or sooner.
Owner: Sam (on-call), eng-runtime (@Alex)

Priya: Customer email short form:

Hi <Customer>,

We detected elevated errors and latency for hosted inference in ap-south1 starting at ~02:05 UTC. Our engineers are deploying mitigations; we are assessing customer impact and any eligibility for service credits. We will follow up with further details.

— Redwood Inference Status

Morgan: For billing we need per-customer contiguous outage minutes. Quick median impacted minutes = 42m, top-impacted median = 1h5m. Contiguous windows over 60 minutes: acct-7721 flagged, acct-1344 borderline at 58 minutes.
Kyle: CSV uploaded: /ops/incident-exports/2162349999-impact.csv. Summary URL: https://internal.redwood/ops/exports/2162349999-summary.csv
Billing Bot: Export ready: /ops/incident-exports/2162349999-impact.csv. Tagging accounts with contiguous >60m: acct-7721.
Sam: Emily (Billing), can you ingest and run the SLA eligibility check? Reminder of policy: contiguous outage >60 minutes OR >0.5% request loss over billing period triggers review.
Emily: Will start run in 45 minutes. We'll prepare estimated credit amounts for flagged accounts and queue communications. ETA for estimates: 2.5 hours.
Alex: Full rollback/promo completed at 02:46 UTC. Post-mitigation metrics: error rate <0.6% across region, p95 latency returned to baseline. Root cause prelim: unbounded KV cache growth under long streaming sessions combined with slower pod churn; autoscaler cooldown parameters delayed replacement. Opening follow-up ticket for autoscaler tuning and model-level KV caps.
Sam: Action items: eng-runtime (Alex) — autoscaler tuning + enforce per-session KV caps; eng-ml (Morgan) — model config limits for long-context streaming; Product (Priya) — customer comms and post-incident writeup; Billing (Emily) — credit calc and outbound. Add owners and ETAs to the incident ticket.
Priya: Proposed customer credit message (to be sent after Billing confirms):

Hi <Customer>,

We completed our investigation into the disruption on 2026-03-15. Our analysis shows your account experienced ~X minutes of degraded requests. Per the Redwood Inference SLA, we are issuing a credit of Y% for the affected billing period. Credits will appear on your next invoice. If you have questions, please reply to this message.

Regards,
Redwood Inference Support

Sam: Don’t include preliminary credit numbers in the public status update. Use: "We are evaluating eligibility for service credits and will notify impacted customers." Priya updated the statuspage accordingly.
Incident Bot: Severity downgraded to Sev3 at 2026-03-15T03:05:12Z — bulk error rate reduced and fallback in place.
Alex: Attached quick-change diff used for fallback (for RCA):

```n- modelVersion: v3-large
+ modelVersion: v2-small
  maxContextTokens: 10240
  kvCacheRetention: aggressive
```n
Morgan: Adding logs and traffic replay snippets to the follow-up ticket.
Kyle: Final per-account impact summary refreshed here: https://internal.redwood/ops/exports/2162349999-final.csv
Emily: Billing will start applying credits once we've validated the CSV and had comms approved. Target: enqueue credits in next billing cycle (within 5 business days).
Sam: We'll publish a postmortem within 72 hours with root cause and mitigation plan. Closing live mitigation. Reopen if any regression appears. :white_check_mark:
Incident Bot: Incident closed at 2026-03-15T03:30:00Z.
